newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end weaker after disappointing day.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end weaker after disappointing day.

text.p: * NZ share market ignores Dow rise to finish weaker
* Good volumes traded in CIL following Australian sale
* Market looking to Telecom, Carter results next week
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index -8.85 at 2,312.26

New Zealand's share market finished the week with a soft tone on Friday after a lethargic session.
A 51 point rise in the Dow Jones Industrial Index was largely ignored, with the NZ Top 40 Capital Index finishing 8.85 points weaker at 2,312.26.
Volumes were light but worth a reasonable NZ$59.5 million.
"A very disappointing day in our market. Turnover was pretty skinny really. In terms of dollars it was alright, but it was just incredibly quiet," said First New Zealand Capital broker Jim Patterson.
Fletcher Paper was the only stock on the leaderboard to notch up a rise, finishing up three at NZ$3.28.

Corporate Investments ended two cents stronger at 73 cents after trading briefly to 74 cents as the company announced it had entered into a contract to sell Fifty Cavill Avenue Pty in Australia, for $52 million.
A total of 4.6 million CIL shares were crossed, worth $3.3 million.
"The Cavill Avenue sale was obviously received reasonably well -- that's been a bit of a millstone for them," Patterson said.
Triumph Industries gained eight cents on the day to close at 73 cents after reporting an unaudited pre-tax profit of $725,000 for the first quarter.
Carter Holt Harvey slipped away at the close to finish four cents lower at $3.22, after initially trading down 10 cents and recovering temporarily to $3.24.
Analysts expect low commodity prices and increased competition in packaging to almost halve Carter's annual profit to around $235 million when it reports its results next week.
